text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- Hungary should tighten conditions attached to agricultural export subsidies, whose allocation now often goes unchecked, government ministers concurred at Thursday's cabinet session, agreeing that the compenent ministers should prepare recommendations by early fall on solutions to the problem.
- Private pension funds will be able to begin operation in September.
- Banks must effect credit transfers within one day based on a July 10 decree from the central bank.
- The cabinet approved the privatisation in several stages of the Hungarian airlines Malev Rt at its Thursday meeting.

- The Euromoney magazine has rated CIB Hungaria as the best Hungarian bank, the brokerage firm Concorde as best share trader and fund management company, and Creditanstalt as best foreign securities firm active in Hungary.
- The broadcasting company Antenna Hungarian Rt is expected to bid for utilization of certain network elements of the alternative telecommunications company MKM-Tel Kft.

- The Free Democrats must leave the governing coalition soon if they hope to reverse their weakened position in the run-up to the 1998 elections, Miklos Tamas Gaspar, a Free Democrat founding member and former MP is cited as saying.

- No political force should be allowed to jeopardize Hungary's chances for accession to NATO in the interests of "narrow political goals" in the run-up to this fall's non-binding referendum on the issue, an opposition MP on Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee told a Thursday news conference.

- Hungary's experience of kicking a lagging economy into gear is of key interest to Peru as the government in Lima prepares to expand its ties with Budapest for the first time in 25 years, a senior Peruvian MP says in an interview with the daily.
- The Ministry of Agriculture has kept to its scheduled utilisation of annual financial resources in the first half of the year, ministry state secretary Fulop Benedek said.
- The number of savings cooperatives dropped to 247 forom 249 as a result of mergers last year, reports the State Money and Capital Market Supervision.
- The government will propose to Parliament that investors in underdeveloped regions of Hungary receive a 100 percent tax exemption for ten years.
